message.abstract:
<jats:title>A topological paradigm shift</jats:title>
          <jats:p>The discovery of topological phases of matter forced condensed matter physicists to question and reexamine some of the basic notions of their discipline. Wen reviews the progress of the field that took a sharp turn from Landau's broken symmetry paradigm to arrive at the modern notions of topological order and quantum entanglement in many-body systems. This development was made possible by using increasingly sophisticated mathematical formalisms.</jats:p>
          <jats:p>
            <jats:italic>Science</jats:italic>
            , this issue p.

          </jats:p>
